capabilities: Edit notes with Helix keymap, selections, multiple cursors, registers, macros, undo tree, text objects, surround and jump labels
Configure keys and options through a helix.toml file copied from an existing Helix config
Trigger Obsidian commands from Helix keys, such as opening the quick switcher or following links
Move cursors and selections across Live Preview table cells
Show available keys in a menu when pressing Space or g
disambiguation: Not just cursor motions; it ports Helix's full editing model, including selections, registers, macros, surround and jump labels.
extras: Requires Obsidian 1.15 or later on desktop; users must turn off Vim key bindings and other Vim plugins. Commands needing a shell, language server or debugger are not supported. Detailed scope and command lists live in docs/scope.md rather than the README.
problem: Obsidian's built-in modal editing only supports Vim keys, so Helix users cannot use their existing keymap, selections and muscle memory in the app.

relations.evidence: The Helix engine is ported from Helix at commit a714a818a3
The way to end IME composition in normal mode comes from codemirror-vim

summary: Modal editor that brings Helix's keymap, selections, multiple cursors and config file to Obsidian notes.
